entries.description: for router server, whether to automatically load models (default: enabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_AUTOLOAD)
entries.notes: Same spelling pair (--models-autoload / --no-models-autoload), env binding, and enabled default. With autoload off, a request naming an unloaded model answers b10621's 400 "model is not loaded"; the per-request ?autoload= query override is honored exactly as upstream's is_autoload reads it (true/1).

entries.description: directory containing models for the router server (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR)
entries.notes: Since #1438 the flag carries b10621's router semantics: with no model argument it starts router mode over the directory (in-process model pool, discovery of checkpoint directories, load/unload/SSE routes, autoload, models-max LRU). The pre-#1438 mlxcel meaning (local model-store root) moved to the mlxcel-native --model-store-root / MLXCEL_MODELS_DIR.
divergence: Combining --models-dir with a model argument fails startup with a migration diagnostic naming --model-store-root; b10621 accepts the flag as inert outside router mode. The refusal protects deployments that relied on the flag's pre-#1438 mlxcel store-root meaning (#1438).

Router mode serves models in-process rather than as child llama-server processes, so the model objects' status.args argv list is empty and no child loaded_info keys are merged into GET /models entries (#1438).

rationale.reason: Combining --models-dir with a model argument is exactly the flag's pre-#1438 mlxcel store-root use, and honoring either meaning silently would change behavior under an operator's feet, so it fails with the map to --model-store-root (pinned by models_dir_with_a_model_argument_fails_startup_with_the_migration_map in src/server/cli_input_tests.rs). The empty status.args argv follows from router mode serving models in-process rather than as child llama-server processes, an architectural property that leaves no child argv to report.
rationale.revisit_if: the migration guard could be retired in a major release once no supported deployment still reads --models-dir as the store root; the in-process empty argv is architectural and would remain.

entries.description: for router server, maximum number of models to load simultaneously (default: 4, 0 = unlimited) (env: LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_MAX)
entries.notes: Same spelling, env binding, and default (4, 0 = unlimited). In router mode the cap is enforced with least-recently-used eviction of loaded models when a load would exceed it; a pool whose running entries are all still loading answers 503 instead of thrashing. Validated with two real checkpoints cycling through load, eviction, and reload in the #1438 PR.

entries.description: path to INI file containing model presets for the router server (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_PRESET)
entries.notes: Implemented since #1438's cache-source PR: the INI file is parsed with upstream's grammar ([name] sections, [*] global preset cascaded under every model, ; and # comments, version key skipped, unknown keys a startup error), keys accept both the long-option spelling without dashes and the LLAMA_ARG_* environment spelling, and each section overlays a clone of the router's own startup config which is re-resolved through the same pipeline as the CLI, so preset keys and CLI flags cannot drift (explicitly-given router CLI flags win over preset values, upstream's own overlay order). Sections define models via model= (checkpoint directory) or hf-repo= (a cache snapshot), or overlay configuration onto a discovered model; the preset-only load-on-startup, stop-timeout, and dedup-cache-models options parse, with load-on-startup and dedup-cache-models honored and stop-timeout inert (in-process unload needs no force-kill escalation). Translated keys: model, hf-repo, alias, tags, ctx-size, parallel, temp, top-k, top-p, min-p, seed, n-predict.
divergence: Keys outside the translated set fail startup with a diagnostic naming the key and section; b10621 can apply any server option per model. The refusal is the epic's no-silent-ignore rule, and the translated set grows with mlxcel's per-model configurability (#1438).
A preset hf-repo= must already be a cache snapshot at startup; b10621 downloads a preset's hf-repo on demand when the model loads (#1438).

entries.description: set model tags, comma-separated (informational, not used for routing) (env: LLAMA_ARG_TAGS)
entries.notes: Comma-separated informational tags, split with the same trim/sort/de-dup rule as --alias and reported in the /v1/models model object's tags array; never used for routing, exactly upstream's contract.

Implemented since #1438's cache-source PR: a cache-sourced model is removed from disk (an in-flight download is cancelled first, a loaded instance unloaded first), the entry leaves the list, and the SSE stream carries model_remove. The refusal surface matches upstream exactly: a missing name answers 400 "model must be a non-empty string", an unknown one 500 "model name=X is not found", and a models-dir or preset entry 500 "model name=X is not removable (not from cache)". Deletion is containment-checked against the store root (the same sanitized <owner>/<name> composition and re-assertion the mlxcel rm verb uses), so an HTTP-supplied name can never delete outside the cache.

Router mode serves the SSE stream with b10621's event envelope ({"model", "event"[, "data"]}) and, since #1438's cache-source PR, the full event vocabulary: models_reload, model_status on load begin, status_change on load/unload transitions, download_progress with per-url {done, total} while POST /models fetches into the cache, download_finished / download_failed at each download's end, and model_remove when DELETE /models removes a cache entry.
divergence: status_change payloads carry no child exit_code and no child /props-derived info block for loaded models: router mode serves models in-process, so there is no child process to exit or to report loading facts over a pipe. Download progress info is served; the child-lifecycle payload fields have no in-process referent (#1438).

rationale.reason: The in-process pool is the same architectural property already argued on --models-dir: models are served inside mlxcel-server rather than as child llama-server processes, so a process exit code and a child's self-reported loading info do not exist to be forwarded. Fabricating an exit_code for a load that never had a process would be less honest than omitting the field.

entries.notes: Implemented since #1438's cache-source PR: the name is validated (non-empty, well-formed repo id, synchronous metadata probe against the hub, exactly upstream's validate-then-download order), an existing name answers 400 "model 'X' already exists", a missing one 400 "model must be a non-empty string", and a valid new one answers {"success": true} while a background task downloads the MLX snapshot into the model cache (the mlxcel store that --model-store-root / MLXCEL_MODELS_DIR / MLXCEL_CACHE_DIR resolve). The transient entry is listed with status "downloading" and per-url progress, the SSE stream carries download_progress / download_finished / download_failed, and a finished snapshot lists as a removable cache entry.
divergence: A bare, owner-less model name expands to mlxcel's default organization (mlx-community/<name>) before validation and download, the same expansion -m <name> and mlxcel download apply, so the cache entry lists under the expanded repo id where b10621 lists the verbatim name (#1438).

rationale.reason: mlxcel's model-reference domain is uniform across every surface that accepts a repo id (-m, mlxcel download, the store layout, and POST /models): a bare name means <default-org>/<name> everywhere, and the store's <owner>/<name> layout has exactly one spelling for each snapshot. Accepting a verbatim owner-less id on this one route would create cache entries the rest of mlxcel cannot name. Pinned by post_models_expands_bare_names_to_the_default_org in src/server/router_server_tests.rs.
rationale.revisit_if: mlxcel's model-reference resolution stops expanding bare names, or the store gains a verbatim-id layout addressable by the other surfaces.

entries.notes: Router mode: an unknown model answers upstream's 404 "model is not found", a running one its 400 "model is already running", and a successful begin answers {"success": true} while the load proceeds through loading to loaded, observable on GET /models and the SSE stream.

Router mode: an unknown model answers 400 "model is not found", a not-running one 400 "model is not running", and success answers {"success": true}. Unload is graceful by refcount: in-flight requests hold the model's serving state until they finish, then the worker exits and the weights free.
